name: mint_pod
description:
Persist provided content as a durable pod and return its pod_id. Use this when asked to 'make/save a datapod' from information you already have (a list, a note, a set of contacts) — it writes a real pod_store row so the content survives the turn and can be reopened later by pod_id. This is NOT for files on disk (use mint_pod_from_path) and NOT pod search (use pod_search).

Returns the canonical pod_id (datapod:note:...). ALWAYS surface that id back to the user / downstream so the pod can be reopened with pod_fetch. If you only have a spec and don't call this tool, nothing is persisted.

inputs.name: body
inputs.description: Full content, stored verbatim as the pod body.

inputs.name: kind
inputs.description: Pod kind; only 'note' is allowed (the default).

inputs.name: tags
inputs.description: Optional tag names for later pod_search filtering.

inputs.name: importance
inputs.description: Optional curation importance 0-10 (higher surfaces first). Omit if unsure.

inputs.name: min_authority
inputs.description: Read-permission band (10 public / 50 chat / 70 gated / 99 user-only). Default 50.

arguments_prompt:
Persist content as a pod and get back its pod_id.

Fields:
  - `title` — one-line summary (becomes one_liner).
  - `body` — the full content, stored verbatim.
  - `tags` (optional) — for pod_search.
  - `min_authority` (optional) — 10 public / 50 chat (default) / 70 gated / 99 user-only.

Returns `pod_id` (datapod:note:...). Surface it back so the pod can be reopened with pod_fetch.

Example:
  `{ "title": "Friends & Family Emails", "body": "Alice: alice@example.com\nBob: bob@example.com", "tags": ["contacts"] }`
